_source_note: PDF content reframed for generic PC GTM (no Steam/Valve/Mad Octopus refs). 9 phases grouped into 5 slides for clarity. T-offsets are in months unless noted as 'd' (days). Used by render_roadmap.py with --release-date to compute calendar dates.

slides.title: Foundations & Identity
slides.subtitle: Lay the legal, creative, and audience groundwork.

sections.heading: Phase 0 — Business & Game Readiness
items: Legal entity formed; business bank account opened; tax forms ready.
Platform listing fee budgeted ($100 per title on most PC storefronts).
Trademark search on working title; primary domain secured.
IP rights audit — every asset has a paper trail or clean license.
Vertical slice playable: core loop demonstrable in under 5 minutes.
Working title, genre, and 5 store-page tags locked.
Target audience defined in one sentence — actionable, not aspirational.

sections.heading: Phase 1 — Audience & Identity
items: 20 comparable titles analyzed: tags, price, review count, themes.
50+ reviews of nearest 3 comps mined for love-it / hate-it patterns.
Communities mapped: 10 subreddits, 5 Discords, 3 forums where target audience lives.
3 wishful comps named (“For fans of X meets Y”) — your positioning compass.
One-sentence hook drafted and pressure-tested with 10 strangers.
Visual identity: logo, key art direction, palette, and font choices locked.

slides.title: Store Page & Audience Building
slides.subtitle: Ship the page that converts and start filling the funnel.

sections.heading: Phase 2 — Store Page Foundations
items: Platform backend configured: partner account, payee, tax, banking, age gate.
Required visuals: capsules (small/main/vertical), 5–10 screenshots, 2–3 GIFs, 60–90s trailer.
Page copy: short description (300 chars), long description with structured sections.
Pre-launch features enabled: announce date, demo plan, community hub.
First-wave press kit: 1-page fact sheet, hi-res key art, gameplay clips, contact.

sections.heading: Phase 3 — Audience Building
items: Community channels live: Discord, X/social, dev blog, mailing list.
Content cadence: 12 weeks of weekly devlog / GIF / screenshot posts pre-built.
Outreach: 50 curators, 30 press contacts, 30 streamers researched and tiered.
Wishlist milestones tracked: 1K (validation), 7K (signal), 25K (healthy launch).
Target 15K–30K wishlists by launch — the band most genre titles need.

slides.title: Demo Fest & Pre-Launch Push
slides.subtitle: Convert attention into wishlists, then convert wishlists into buyers.

sections.heading: Phase 4 — Demo Showcase Fest
items: Demo build polished to 30–90 min of best-foot-forward gameplay; first 5 min hook tested.
Festival registration completed early; capsule and demo trailer submitted on spec.
Pre-fest push: socials, newsletter, Discord countdown; 3 streamers lined up.
During fest: daily metrics review (CTR, demo D/L, wishlist uplift), reply to every review.
Post-fest: thank-you devlog, list of fixes, demo stays up if rules allow.

sections.heading: Phase 5 — Pre-Launch Push
items: Launch trailer (60–90s) cut; first 5s hook validated; release date + CTA in end card.
Trailer mirrored in native ratios: 16:9 (YouTube), 1:1 (X), 9:16 (TikTok/Reels).
Embargoed review keys to top 20 press, 4 weeks out; 30 personalized streamer emails.
Final build to default branch 2 weeks before launch; day-1 patch staged separately.
Achievements, save-cloud, controller, localization, handheld cert all tested.
Paid test (optional): $500–$2K across Meta/TikTok/YouTube/Reddit, 3 creative angles.

slides.title: Launch Week & Launch Day
slides.subtitle: Be present. Respond fast. Don’t break anything.

sections.heading: Phase 6 — Launch Week
items: T-7: Final QA pass by fresh eyes; pricing locked; 10% launch discount decided.
T-7: Press release (short, scannable, assets attached) sent 48h pre-launch under embargo.
T-3: Server capacity checked across Discord, site, support email; on-call rota covers 16+ hrs.
T-3: Pre-written launch posts and common-bug response templates approved.
T-1: Sleep schedule planned; final wishlist count screenshotted; tools and devices tested.

sections.heading: Phase 7 — Launch Day
items: Hr 0–2: Confirm release went live (refresh, check backend); launch posts on all channels within 30 min.
Hr 2–8: Reply to every review and Discord ping; pin known issues; hotfix only critical bugs.
Hr 8–24: Compile day-1 metrics (wishlist conversion, refund rate, review score, peak CCU).
Day 1 close: Public end-of-day post — thank players, acknowledge issues, set day-2 expectations.
First 7 days: Daily patch notes; re-pitch the 50 streamers who passed pre-launch.

slides.title: Post-Launch Growth
slides.subtitle: Launch is the start, not the finish. Months 2–12 often beat month 1.

sections.heading: Phase 8a — First 30 Days
items: Major patch addressing top community concerns shipped.
First platform featured-deal slot applied for; aim for ≥25% discount.
Festival applications: indie showcases, genre fests, summer/winter events.
Console-port decision gated at ~5K PC units sold; porting partners scoped (6–12 mo lead).

sections.heading: Phase 8b — Months 2–12
items: Monthly free content updates — each one a visibility refresh on the platform.
Discount cadence: 3 major sales + 1–2 mid-cycle drops planned.
Localization expansion based on regional sales (Brazilian PT, Simplified Chinese typically highest ROI).
Cross-promo bundles with adjacent-genre devs; re-engagement campaign for lapsed wishlists.
Months 6–12: Major DLC / 1.0 if Early Access; awards push; public post-mortem; planning game #2 begins.
